title: Payment lifecycle and flows
idea: The payment lifecycle is a state machine: a Payment moves from CREATED through PROCESSING to SUCCEEDED or FAILED, and only successful payments can be refunded.
points: PROCESSING ends in SUCCEEDED or FAILED, decided by the gateway, not a timer.
SUCCEEDED moves to PARTIALLY_REFUNDED or REFUNDED as refunds add up.
FAILED and REFUNDED are final; nothing may leave them.
A repeated webhook is ignored; a conflicting one raises an alert.

hero.title: A UPI payment, end to end

messages.label: pay(ORD-1, UPI, k-1)
messages.note: The customer pays by UPI. A Payment P-1 is CREATED for key k-1.

messages.label: collect(P-1, 49900)
messages.note: The service sends a collect request and moves P-1 to PROCESSING.

messages.label: accepted, pending
messages.note: The gateway accepted the request but has no final answer yet.

messages.label: P-1 PROCESSING
messages.note: The app asks the customer to approve in their UPI app and starts polling.

messages.label: approve 49900?
messages.note: The customer's UPI app shows the request. The customer approves it.

messages.label: approved
messages.note: The approval reaches the gateway through the UPI network.

messages.label: webhook: SUCCEEDED
messages.note: The service verifies the webhook signature, then moves PROCESSING to SUCCEEDED.

messages.label: webhook: SUCCEEDED
messages.note: Webhooks may arrive more than once. The second one is ignored as a duplicate.

messages.label: GET /payments/P-1
messages.note: The next poll returns SUCCEEDED and the app shows the receipt.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Payment asks the enum before every change.

walk.text: P-1: happy path, a duplicate webhook, a partial refund, then a full refund.
P-2 fails, then a late SUCCEEDED event arrives.
An EnumMap lists allowed next states. CREATED may fail before any gateway call; FAILED and REFUNDED have none.
`canMoveTo` is the single question every change asks.
Same status again without a self-loop is a duplicate: ignore it quietly.
Any other illegal move is refused and needs a person to look.
A legal move updates the status and the history.

pitfalls: Do not mark a payment FAILED on timeout; wait for the webhook or reconciler.
Verify the webhook signature before trusting the status it carries.
Never set status directly; every change goes through `moveTo`.

quiz.q: What does PaymentLifecycle print for P-2's late SUCCEEDED?
quiz.why: FAILED has no allowed next states. SUCCEEDED differs from FAILED, so it is not a duplicate, and `moveTo` prints the refusal.

takeaway: Allowed moves live in one enum; duplicates are ignored, conflicts alerted.

starters: What should happen to money when a FAILED payment later succeeds?
